question: Sell a single-tenant Jack in the Box (NNN, Central Los Angeles, expiry window 2030-2035) before the lease expires, or renew and hold — for an owner whose priorities are wealth preservation with a manageable level of risk and room for growth.
normalization: The owner's contract rent, basis and debt are private and blank (flags F-01, F-05). Every number below is therefore published on an index basis: value = 1.00 equals one year of current net operating income (NOI). Dollar outcomes scale linearly with actual NOI. No private fact was assumed.

strategies.name: HOLD — renew/extend the NNN lease and keep the asset to and beyond expiry
strategies.summary: Negotiate renewal now (2026-2028) with CPI-linked escalators above metro ECI (3.9% YoY, S01), then hold to the 2030-2035 window and either renew again or sell at expiry.
pros: Captures contracted income while area labor market improves (county unemployment 4.8% SA, S02)
Defers all transfer-tax friction (ULA 4.45% if in City limits, S10)
Defers capital-gains tax indefinitely while 10-year Treasury yields 4.86% (S08)
cons: Single-tenant concentration: tenant SSS -1.1% and elevated closures into 2028 (S04)
Structural demand headwinds: county population -3.2% since 2020 (S03), K-12 enrollment -240,800 by 2035-36 (S30)
Carries 100% of earthquake (60% in 30 yrs, S13) and wildfire (S14/S15) exposure on one parcel

strategies.name: SELL before expiry (target closing 2027-2029) and diversify into a broad portfolio
strategies.summary: Run a sale process now against the official net-lease benchmark (6.8% initial cash yield, Q3 2026, S07), pay transfer tax and any capital-gains tax, and reinvest net proceeds in a diversified income portfolio.
pros: Removes single-tenant and single-parcel black-swan exposure (R17, R18, R20)
Locks a price while the official benchmark yield is 6.8% and benchmark occupancy 98.8%
Converts a declining-population county asset into diversified exposure
cons: ULA adds 4.45% (tier 1) or 5.95% (tier 2) of gross consideration if the parcel is in City limits (S10)
Capital-gains tax depends on private basis (F-10) — deferred if §1031 is used instead
Sells into a market where the tenant's brand is shrinking (S04)

strategies.name: EXCHANGE — sell before expiry and roll proceeds via IRC §1031 into diversified NNN real estate
strategies.summary: Same timing as SELL, but replacement property of equal or greater value is acquired within the 45/180-day framework (S16), deferring federal capital-gains tax; transfer tax still applies at sale.
pros: Keeps real-estate exposure (no forced portfolio change) while diversifying away from one parcel/one tenant
Defers capital-gains tax: gain is 'deferred, not forgiven' (S16)
Benchmark shows institutional net-lease demand is deep: 15,536-asset benchmark portfolio at 98.8% occupancy (S07)
cons: 45-day identification and 180-day close are hard deadlines — only extendable in a presidentially declared disaster (S16)
ULA transfer tax is NOT deferred by §1031 — it is a tax on conveyance (S10)
Reinvestment at today's benchmark yield (6.8%) may be below the asset's going-in cap if the market tightens

strategies.name: HOLD-TO-EXPIRY then SELL at expiry (2030-2035 grid)
strategies.summary: Keep the lease through expiry and sell in the expiry year; the model publishes a 2030-2035 grid of exit-cap outcomes on the index basis.
pros: Optionality: sell at expiry with no pre-expiry vacancy risk if re-tenanting is avoided
cons: Exposes the full terminal value to the 2030-2035 cap-rate and local-demand path
Tenant may not renew (R01/R02/R20), leaving a rollover sale instead of a income sale

model_evidence.index_basis: 1.00 = one year of current NOI; horizon end-2040; seed 20261110; 10,000 trials
model_evidence.reading: Holding wins on expected wealth (+8.3 index units) only because the asset's ~6.8% yield exceeds the officially anchored 4.86% reinvestment anchor. Selling/exchanging wins on risk-adjusted wealth: the worst-5% outcome is 5.1 index units better, and the chance of an idiosyncratic loss above 10 index units falls from 8.9% to 0.01%. The break-even reinvestment rate for the base 2032 case is 7.06%: below that, holding is the expected-value winner; above it, selling wins outright. The user's stated objective (wealth preservation with growth at manageable risk) is therefore served by ranking the risk-adjusted winner first, with the hold case retained as the expected-value benchmark and the triggers as the switching rules.

recommendation.headline: NEGOTIATE FIRST, PRICE SECOND: extend/renew the lease on CPI-linked terms in 2026-2028 while the local labor market is strong, run a parallel disciplined sale process with a reserve price set above break-even, and execute a §1031 exchange if either (a) the best bid clears break-even after the 4.45% City transfer stack, or (b) the owner weighs the risk-adjusted case — the model shows diversifying improves the worst-5% outcome by 5.1 index units at a cost of 8.3 index units of expected wealth.

ranking.why: Risk-adjusted winner in the model: CVaR5 21.1 vs 16.0 for holding, and P(idiosyncratic loss > 10 index units) falls from 8.9% to 0.01%. Keeps real-estate income exposure (growth) while removing single-parcel black swans (60% quake in 30 yrs, twin Jan-2025 fires) and the single-tenant bet on a brand with -1.1% SSS (O11), and defers capital-gains tax under S16. Cost: 8.3 index units of expected wealth versus holding.

Expected-value winner (mean 33.9 vs 25.7) because the ~6.8% asset yield beats the officially anchored 4.86% reinvestment rate — but only while renewal terms are strong (escalators >= metro ECI 3.9%, S01) and tenant credit holds (S04). Population and school-age trajectories (S03, S30) argue against a passive hold into 2035.
Same exit logic as rank 1 but pays capital-gains tax now on unknown basis (F-10); dominated by S-EXCHANGE unless the owner wants out of real estate entirely.
Highest terminal-value variance: the whole bet sits on 2030-2035 cap rates in a county losing population. Acceptable only as the outcome of a failed renewal negotiation, not as a plan.

conditions: If the best bid (net of 4.45%/5.95% City transfer stack and closing costs) exceeds hold-value at the model's base break-even cap, sell/exchange.
If the tenant offers renewal with escalators >= metro ECI (3.9% YoY, S01) and the renewal term runs past 2032, hold through the extension and re-price in 2030.
If tenant SSS falls again for a second consecutive fiscal year, or guidance turns to net system closures above 100/yr, move to rank 1 immediately regardless of price (R01, R02).
If earthquake coverage cannot be bound at acceptable cost after any fault-map finding, exit via rank 1 (R17, R19).

triggers.trigger: Best bid < base break-even cap on the model's 2027-2029 grid
Best bid > base break-even cap after transfer tax
JACK fiscal-year SSS decline >= 2 consecutive years or FY guidance cut below -3%
Renewal escalator < CPI-U metro (3.7% YoY, S01)
Bound insurance quote rises > 50% vs expiring premium
triggers.action: Re-underwrite hold case; treat as R19 warning

triggers.trigger: SoS certifies Prop 3 differently than the unofficial 60.4% Yes

falsifiers: The recommendation is wrong if the owner's actual basis makes the after-tax cost of selling exceed the single-asset risk premium by a wide margin (basis is blank — F-05/F-10).
The recommendation is wrong if the parcel is outside City of Los Angeles limits (no ULA applies — F-08), which materially lowers exit friction and favors selling sooner.
The recommendation is wrong if the tenant's next fiscal-year SSS turns positive and the closure program ends (R01/R02 reverse).
The recommendation is wrong if the official net-lease benchmark yield moves materially away from 6.8% before execution (S07 is a dated print, 2026-11-02).
